extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / naturalists; readers/contributors to Philosophical Transactions
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting anatomical descriptions, natural-history observations, and small-scale experiments for publication; includes observational detail, experimental procedure, measurements, and practical/husbandry instructions. Emphasis on reproducible method descriptions, comparative remarks, and practical tests (e.g., material quality or animal husbandry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed anatomical description
rubrics_metrics.description: Give accurate, minute descriptions of internal and external anatomy (organs, fibres, vessels, ventricles, spinal marrow, cranium, ovarium, parts of generation, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe substance, shape, fibres, vessels and their progress; note resemblances to other species; enumerate parts and any peculiar structures (e.g. 'the heart reaches from the head to the tail', 'ventricle reaches from one extreme of the worm to the other'). Include vestiges (e.g. remaining silky intestines) and rare perceptible motions (e.g. of the heart).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative measurements and timings
rubrics_metrics.description: Record numerical measurements and timings of observed phenomena (durations, counts, lengths, quantities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report precise values where possible (examples from the text: 'divesting itself of its coat in the space of 1 min. 10 sec.', 'aurelia changes into a butterfly in ten days in summer and a month's time in autumn and winter', 'male beating his wings about 130 times in one copulation', 'eggs amounting to 300, 400, sometimes 500', 'reckoned 930 Bononian feet of silk wound off from one bag'). Give units and conditions (season, temperature) that affect timings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit experimental method and procedural detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide step-by-step procedural descriptions of experiments and manipulations so others can reproduce them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include apparatus details (sizes, shapes), how items are prepared (e.g. heating and sealing a glass bubble), handling steps (breaking sealed end under water with forceps), measures taken to prevent artefacts (ensuring 'no bubble of air appeared to emerge'), and how measurements are collected (counterpoised balances, weights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and uncertainty/accounting for losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat experiments and report consistency and possible sources of discrepancy or loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Boyle repeats the bubble experiment with a larger bubble and reports slight differences, accounting for lost grains due to remaining water or vapours. State replicate results, estimate small losses, and note plausible causes for variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls and observational checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate controls and deliberate checks to isolate effects and test hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: wrapping a chameleon in white linen to test colour change, ensuring no air escapes when breaking a bubble under water, putting animals on differently coloured objects to test colour-taking. Note which manipulations produced effects and which did not (e.g. colour change only with white linen first time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare with prior literature and note discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare observations to previous authors and explicitly note agreements or contradictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite prior claims (e.g. Aristotle or other authors asserting spontaneous generation or anatomical features) and state whether present observations confirm or refute them (e.g. refuting that the chameleon 'takes all colours but white', or not finding a foramen ovale claimed by many authors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional interpretation / physiological inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer plausible functional explanations for observed structures or behaviours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide hypotheses linking form to function (examples: camel stomach sacks as reservoirs to retain water; cutaneous vessel fluid changes explaining chameleon colour changes; vessels of silk explaining different sorts of webs). Distinguish observation from conjecture where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical instructions for husbandry and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Give actionable, procedural guidance for handling, breeding, or processing biological materials (eggs, silk bags, breeds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ways of keeping eggs and ordering them for hatching, the manner of winding off silk bags, and how many threads together make good silk. Give steps and expected outcomes (e.g. amount of silk per bag).

rubrics_metrics.name: Material-quality tests with clear diagnostic criteria (slate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide simple, reproducible tests and interpretive criteria to judge material quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For slate: 'take and strike it against any hard body; then if the sound be distinct and clear, that sort of stone is firm and good.' Additional tests: hewing to see if it breaks before the edge, weighing before and after immersion to detect water absorption (gain after 2–8 hours signals porosity), inspecting colour (deep blackish blue apt to take in water; lighter blue firmer), touch/texture (good stone feels hard and rough; bad stone smooth/oily), vertical immersion to observe capillary draw (good stone draws water only up ~½ inch at edges; bad stone draws to the top). State interpretation thresholds where given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitat, behaviour, and seasonality reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Document locations, microhabitats, behaviours and seasonal timing of organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example details: snail species found under loose bark of willows or in elm/oak clefts; spiders darting and 'sailing' by issuing threads in summer/September, fewer in winter; snails pairing in March. Include locality, seasonal differences, and behavior context (e.g. aerial prey capture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus description and precautions for measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe apparatus geometry and precautions affecting measurements so others can judge reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from Boyle's work: glass bubble size (egg-sized or hen-egg-sized), stem turned up to break off, heating to rarefy air, tying to a lead weight and balance, use of long iron forceps to break bubble underwater. Note that apparatus shape and handling influence results and losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record species variation and geographic differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Note differences among species and between geographic populations when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Mexican chameleons do not show the same eye motion; a Sicilian butterfly is twice fecund in one year (April and August). Always report locality and any observed variant traits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sensory/tactile diagnostics in observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ and report simple sensory tests (sight, touch, sound) as diagnostic evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: observing colour changes in sunlight/shade and after touch, feeling slate texture (hard/rough vs smooth/oily), listening to slate when struck. Describe the test and the qualitative cues used to judge quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative morphology across species
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare anatomical features across species to highlight distinctive adaptations or resemblances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: beaver fore feet resembling man's hands, hind feet like a goose; differences in bear vs lion guts and kidneys; note counts (ribs, length of guts) and special structures (multiple small kidneys). Use such comparisons to suggest function or natural history significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear narrative sequencing of observations and experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Present observations and experimental steps in a lucid chronological/orderly narrative so readers can follow what was done and seen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the order of operations, times, and transitions (e.g. dissect then observe moving parts; heat then seal then submerge the bubble then break it). Where practical include times of day, dates/seasons, and who performed actions when relevant.
